name: PHerc0009B_20250919123506
description: The segment on which the exact chunk-shell planner earns its keep: a 589 GB volume rendered from a 6.4 GB download on a laptop. This is the reference case for the 1.392x over-fetch measurement in RESULTS.md (R2).
notes: PLAN BEFORE RENDERING. The naive per-tile bounding box asks for 9.28 GB, over a 7.5 GB budget; the exact shell asks for 6.67 GB and fits. Planning costs ~1.2 minutes and fetches zero bytes of volume data.

READ THE OUTPUT WITH TWO MASKS. The renderer's mask is mesh validity, not material presence: 7.04 % of nominally valid pixels (2.31 Mpx, 173 mm2, dominated by one 170 mm2 hole) have all 31 layers at zero, because the auto-grown mesh wanders off the sheet. Mesh-mask area 24.47 cm2 is INFLATED; the honest effective-mask figure is 22.75 cm2.
Calibrating a statistical null on the inflated mask biases it (z_mos 3.52 -> 2.67-3.19). Always calibrate on the effective mask (validity AND mean_z > 0).
Segments share chunks: the union of the top 8 meshes is 26.89 GB against a naive sum of 55.81 GB. Plan a multi-segment set jointly, not one at a time.
The fine 2.401 um scan of this sample is out of reach by this method: 705 GB of shell out of a 23.2 TB volume.
